'''''Galium verrucosum''''', common name '''warty bedstraw''' (US) or '''southern cleavers''' (UK), is a species of plants in the [[Rubiaceae]]. The epithet ''"verrucosum"'' means "warty" in reference to the numerous bumps on the mature fruit. It is native to the [[Mediterranean Basin]] from [[Portugal]] and [[Morocco]] to [[Turkey]] and [[Palestine (region)|Palestine]]. It is reportedly naturalized in [[Great Britain]], [[Central Europe]] (from [[Switzerland]] to [[Poland]]), the [[Canary Islands]], [[Madeira]], and [[Wayne County, Michigan|Wayne County]] ([[Michigan]]).<ref name="bernadettegansert">[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=87859|World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Galium%20verrucosum.png Biota of North America Program]</ref><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=galium+verrucosum Altervista Flora Italiana]</ref>
